column3: The Hebrew says each man took “his censer” and calls the fire “strange,” adding that the LORD “had not commanded them.” BSB uses plural “their censers,” calls the fire “unauthorized,” and says “contrary to His command.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew introduces what the LORD “spoke,” without explicitly saying “meant.” BSB adds that explanatory verb and renders the holiness and honor clauses with active “show” and “reveal.”
The Hebrew calls the dead men “your brothers”; BSB specifies “your cousins” and adds “the bodies.”
The Hebrew says they carried them “in their tunics”; BSB adds “still.”

The Hebrew says “your heads,” without explicitly naming hair, and leaves the subject of becoming angry unnamed; BSB specifies “your hair” and “the LORD.” The Hebrew also repeats the burning word in “the burning which the LORD burned.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew has both “spoke” and “saying”; BSB condenses these to “said.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew lists “the unclean” before “the clean”; BSB reverses their order.
The Hebrew says the LORD “spoke” the statutes “by the hand of Moses”; BSB says He “has given” them “through Moses.”
The Hebrew calls the offering “holiness of holinesses”; BSB says “most holy.”
Close to the Hebrew.

The Hebrew calls the recipients’ portions “your portion and the portion of your sons”; BSB generalizes the second group to “your children.” It says a “clean place,” without the explicit qualifier “ceremonially.”
The Hebrew specifies “your sons with you”; BSB uses the broader “your children” and omits “with you.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew uses an active “He gave it to you” and the image of bearing the congregation’s guilt; BSB uses passive “it was given to you” and “take away the guilt.”
The Hebrew introduces the statement with “Behold,” rather than “Since,” and emphatically repeats the eating verb in the instruction.
The Hebrew asks whether eating would be good “in the eyes of the LORD”; BSB says “acceptable in the sight of the LORD.”
The Hebrew says it was good “in his eyes”; BSB says he “was satisfied” and supplies “this explanation” as what Moses heard.
